There is no Terraform workaround because the Terraform provider performs the same API call and needs the same permission. Re-running the same onboarding command after the policy update is safe and idempotent.

{"body":"Hi Samuel,

I checked the cluster telemetry first: the CAST AI agent is online and node telemetry is flowing, so the cluster side is healthy. We reproduced the failure in a sandbox — a deployer role whose policy lacks iam:PutRolePolicy gets a 403 AccessDenied during the connect run, exactly matching your report.

Per the documentation, the missing permission is iam:PutRolePolicy (add GetRolePolicy and DeleteRolePolicy as well so repeated runs stay idempotent), scoped to arn:aws:iam::951463557399:role/cast-*. There is no Terraform workaround: the Terraform provider performs the same API call and needs the same permission.

After the policy update, re-running the same onboarding command is safe — it reuses the already-created role and policy. Our tests pass against the updated policy in the sandbox.

— CAST AI Support"}
